newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Kansas harvest on pace.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Kansas harvest on pace.

text.p: Harvesting of hard red winter wheat continued to be on pace in Kansas on Thursday with grain merchandisers reporting better-than-expected yields per acre in several areas of the state.
"It looks like the wheat has recovered," a Kansas merchandiser said, referring to good weather after the damage the HRW wheat crop suffered during a mid-April freeze.
In central Kansas, yields were running between 50 to 70 bushels per acre, he said.
That was much higher than the 29-bushel-per-acre yield for Kansas in 1996, according to the U.S. Agriculture Department.
In south central Kansas, a grain merchandiser said in some cases, yields were as high as 70 bushels.
"That is not the norm but it is nice to see," he said. "The state as a whole, will probably average 40 to 45 bushels per acre."
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: N=KCBT July. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
